checks.name: Actual LogRGB GLSL branch recovers zero through HDR32 and ignores alpha; window and About retain sRGB
Day/night decode before linear mixing, with one clock uniform and no reupload at fractional time
A normalized HDR night atlas restores x8 before mixing while daylight, clean intro and unscaled slots retain their original energy
Clean intro uses the same LogRGB decoder before scene blending and one AgX, then removes only its own layer
Invalid LogRGB range/gain are rejected before any texture request or material mutation
Missing physical data disposes parallel partial loads and leaves original materials intact
Missing LogRGB day map releases its successful siblings; caller can dispose the prior physical layer without leaked ownership
A night texture upload failure rolls back partially installed LogRGB day hooks and source color spaces
Missing clean receiver releases only intro textures and retains a usable LogRGB day/night material until caller cleanup
Disposal through a later wrapper cannot revive deleted LogRGB, intro, or reflection resources

scope: Actual production shader composition and ownership, scalar evaluation extracted from the compiled-hook GLSL expression, controlled network/texture-decode/PMREM substitutes. No GPU, browser or ASTC verification is claimed. About remains unchanged.
